messages:
alex: Quick idea dump: instead of a single coalesce window per tenant, model the batch window as an asymmetric waveform (rise, plateau, decay). The scheduler picks parameters based on instantaneous intensity + recent variance. Goal: keep steady low-cost batches for sustained traffic, but collapse latency for sudden spikes.
rhea: waveform layers sound neat. how do we encode them cheaply for the hot path? memcache? inline L1? :memo:
alex: Keep it extremely cheap. L1 in-process map keyed by tenant -> WaveformRef (small struct id+version). Miss => sharded in-mem fallback; rare remote calls. WaveformRef contains shape_id and meta flags only; consult is a single atomic read.
omar: What shape types are we thinking? symmetric gaussian-ish? skewed?
alex: Prototype shapes: 1) Spike (fast rise, short plateau, steep decay), 2) Ramp (slow rise, long plateau), 3) Sustained (flat wide plateau), 4) Bimodal (for bursty patterns). Each shape maps to window_ms_min, window_ms_max, join_budget, deadline_bias.
rhea: Deadline_bias meaning?
alex: Small integer bias applied when evaluating join deadlines: positive bias favors tight latency (prefers immediate dispatch), negative bias favors fill. It nudges admission decision without changing lease semantics.
omar: How about attack surface? tenant pumps fake intensity to get favorable windows.
alex: Mitigations: 1) intensity must be corroborated by server-side observed qps (rolling 30s), mismatch throttles the waveform amplitude. 2) update tokens per tenant are rate-limited (e.g., 1 update/2s). 3) global smoothing: waveform transitions interpolate over X seconds to avoid oscillation.
rhea: KVCACHE interactions? short windows increase cache misses.
alex: Waveform carries warmup_policy: skip | gentle_prefetch | aggressive_prefetch. For Spike shapes we use skip/gentle. Also add eviction_guard: a per-tenant soft floor that raises eviction thresholds when waveform flips to narrow so hot keys aren't evicted mid-session.
omar: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```go
// consult in admission hot path
wf := waveformCache.Get(tenant)
switch wf.ShapeID {
case Spike:
  lease.Timeout = 10ms
  admission.MaxJoin = 6
  kv.Warmup = Skip
case Sustained:
  lease.Timeout = 30ms
  admission.MaxJoin = 24
  kv.Warmup = Aggressive
}
```
alex: Tests + fallbacks: if waveform service fails, fall back to LegacyWindow (current behavior) or a conservative default, depending on a feature flag. We must ensure fallbacks never grant larger windows than legacy.
rhea: Metrics to add: waveform_assigned, waveform_version, waveform_transition_ms, join_attempts, join_rejections_by_deadline, batch_fill_ratio_by_waveform, cluster_level_waveform_imbalance. Also add a debug sampling trace that records consult result for sampled requests.
omar: Rollout plan?
alex: Canary on a single cluster slice for 48h with canary tenants. Collect cost delta and tail latency per-tenant. Add A/B where 10% continue on legacy windows. Safety: auto-rollback if any tenant's batch_latency_p99 > 1.8x or error_rate > baseline+0.5%.
rhea: Session stickiness: important for chat. Propose session_affinity_ttl (default 5m) so a session's waveform choice is sticky and not flipped on every spike. Make it overrideable per-route.
alex: Ops TODOs: feature flag gate, L1 eviction/TTL tuning, RBAC for waveform update API (no external SDKs), dashboard + alert runbook. devx-bot: reminder: add RFC folder + template entry and schedule technical review with runtime + infra.
omar: Edge case: long-tail generation requests (huge token counts) can blow up window assumptions. Might need a separate path that always requests dedicated fastpath or splits into sub-requests.
alex: noted. I'll include a subprotocol for large token requests: require explicit tight-deadline flag from client which opts into narrow-window fastpath or else gets queued under Wide windows.
rhea: Thanks. I'm happy to own the metrics + dashboard.
omar: I'll help with stress tests and abuse simulations.
devx-bot: rfc-draft scheduled in #eng-runtime for review tomorrow 11:00 UTC.
